settings.title: Local Breakdown & Recovery Support in Birmingham

settings.editor:
A.A.D Transport & Recovery is a Birmingham-based vehicle recovery company. We help drivers dealing with a breakdown, vehicle fault, or transportation need quickly, clearly, and without the runaround. Vehicle problems don't send a warning. Whether you're heading to work, driving home, passing through Birmingham, or stuck with a car that just won't start, we're the call you make to sort it out.

Our services centre on three things: roadside recovery, vehicle transportation, and vehicle assessment. From your first call to the job being done, we keep things simple and straightforward  for both urgent breakdowns and planned vehicle moves.

We're based in Birmingham, cover the city and surrounding areas, and we're available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
WHAT WE DO

When your vehicle breaks down or becomes unsafe to drive, getting it somewhere safe is priority one. We help drivers stranded by a breakdown, fault, accident, or anything else that stops a journey in its tracks whether that means help at the roadside or transport to a garage, home, or another destination.

Not every job is an emergency. Sometimes a car just needs moving because it's non-running, needs repairs, or has to get from one place to another. We handle that safely and conveniently, on your schedule.

Not sure what's actually wrong with your vehicle? Our assessment service helps identify faults, defects, and concerns after a breakdown, warning light, or accident so you know exactly what's going on and what needs to happen next. If the vehicle isn't fit to drive, we'll sort recovery or transportation from there.
WHY US

Breakdowns don't wait for convenient timing. Early morning, late at night, weekends, rush hour whenever your vehicle lets you down, we're on call. Emergency breakdown recovery covers any situation where your vehicle has stopped working or isn't safe to drive. Common causes include:

  • Engine or mechanical failure
  • Battery or electrical faults
  • Starting problems
  • Flat or damaged tyres
  • Fuel issues
  • Overheating
  • Dashboard warning lights
  • Accident damage
  • A vehicle that's simply unsafe to drive

Sometimes a quick fix at the roadside gets you back on the road. Other times, your vehicle needs to be recovered and transported to a garage, home, or another location either way, we handle it.

A broken-down car is stressful enough without confusion over what happens next. Our car breakdown recovery service in Birmingham is built to get you moving again with minimum fuss.

We recover vehicles from across the city at home, on local roads, in car parks, or wherever you've come to a stop (subject to safe access). You tell us the situation; we arrange the recovery and get your vehicle where it needs to go, safely and without delay.

Not every breakdown means your car needs transporting.

If it's something like a starting fault that can potentially be sorted at the roadside, we'll try that first. If the vehicle still can't be made safe to drive, we move straight to recovery no unnecessary steps, no confusion about what happens next.

If your vehicle needs professional repair, we'll transport it there directly. You choose the destination:

  • Your local garage
  • A repair centre
  • Your home
  • A dealership
  • Another location of your choice

This is especially useful for non-running vehicles that simply can't be driven anywhere.

A car that won't start can't just be driven onto a truck it needs proper recovery equipment, and that's exactly what we use.

To help us prepare the right equipment before we arrive, let us know:

  • Whether the engine starts
  • Whether the wheels can roll
  • Whether the vehicle is in neutral
  • Whether there's accident damage
  • Whether the vehicle is easily accessible

The more detail you give us, the faster we can get moving.
AFTER AN ACCIDENT

If you've been in a collision, safety comes first. If there's any immediate danger, call the emergency services straight away. Once you and everyone else is safe, we can recover your vehicle from the roadside and transport it to a agreed destination like:

settings.title: What Does a Towing Service in Birmingham Do?

settings.editor:
A towing service helps move a vehicle when it cannot, or should not, be driven to its intended destination.

There are many reasons a driver may need towing. Your vehicle might have suffered a mechanical fault, stopped after a breakdown, been involved in an incident, or simply need transporting to a garage or another safe location.

A professional towing service can provide a safer alternative to attempting to drive a vehicle that may have a serious fault.

At A.A.D Transport & Recovery, we can help with vehicle towing and transportation requirements across Birmingham and surrounding areas. We first need to understand your location, vehicle condition and destination so we can determine the most appropriate recovery or towing solution.

If you are unsure whether your vehicle needs towing or another type of roadside assistance, simply explain the problem when you contact us. We can discuss the situation with you and help determine the next step.

settings.title: When Might You Need Vehicle Towing in Birmingham?

settings.editor:
Not every vehicle problem is the same. Sometimes a minor roadside issue can be resolved without transporting the vehicle, while other situations require the vehicle to be recovered.

You may need a Towing Service Birmingham if:

  • Your vehicle will not start
  • Your car has suffered a mechanical failure
  • The vehicle has lost power and cannot continue safely
  • Your vehicle has broken down on the roadside
  • The car needs to be taken to a garage
  • The vehicle is not suitable or safe to drive
  • Your vehicle has developed a fault away from home
  • You need a non-running vehicle transported
  • A vehicle needs moving after a roadside incident
  • You need your vehicle transported to another suitable location

If you are experiencing a serious vehicle fault, continuing to drive may make the problem worse. If you are unsure whether the vehicle is safe to drive, stop in a safe location where possible and contact a professional recovery service.

settings.title: What Information Should You Give a Towing Company?

settings.editor: When you need a Birmingham Towing Service, having the right information ready can make the conversation easier. Try to provide:

• Your location: Give your exact location, road name or a nearby landmark.
  • Vehicle details: Tell us the make, model and approximate size of the vehicle.
  • Vehicle condition: Explain whether the vehicle starts, moves or has completely stopped.
  • Problem: Tell us what happened before the vehicle became unusable.
  • Destination: Let us know whether you want the vehicle taken home, to a garage, repair centre or another location.
  • Access information: If the vehicle is in a narrow street, underground car park or another restricted area, mention this when booking.

 

The more information you can provide, the easier it is to understand the recovery requirement.

settings.title: Is Towing Safer Than Driving a Faulty Vehicle?

settings.editor:
If a vehicle has a serious mechanical problem, continuing to drive may create additional risks or cause further damage.

For example, if the vehicle is overheating, losing power, making unusual noises or has another major fault, it may be better to stop in a safe location and arrange professional assistance rather than continuing the journey.

If you are uncertain whether your vehicle is safe to drive, contact a recovery professional and explain the symptoms.

A towing service can provide a way to move a vehicle without requiring you to drive it to a garage when driving is not appropriate.

settings.editor:
Flatbed recovery uses a recovery vehicle with a flat loading platform. Instead of travelling on its own wheels, the vehicle is loaded onto the platform and transported to the required destination.

This method can be useful when a vehicle:

  • Will not start
  • Cannot move under its own power
  • Has accident damage
  • Has damaged wheels or tyres
  • Has a serious mechanical fault
  • Should not be driven
  • Needs transporting to a garage
  • Needs moving from one location to another

The appropriate recovery method depends on the vehicle, its condition, location and access. When you contact A.A.D Transport & Recovery, explain what has happened so the recovery requirements can be discussed before transportation is arranged.

settings.title: When Do You Need Flatbed Recovery?

settings.editor: Not every breakdown requires a flatbed recovery vehicle. Some vehicles may be suitable for roadside assistance or another recovery method. However, flatbed transportation can be useful when a vehicle cannot safely be driven.

If your vehicle will not start because of an engine, electrical or mechanical problem, it may need to be transported to a garage. Flatbed recovery provides a way to move the vehicle without requiring it to drive during the journey.

After an accident, a vehicle may have damage to its wheels, steering, suspension or bodywork. Even if the engine starts, the vehicle may not be safe to drive.
Suitable recovery can transport the vehicle to a garage, body shop or another agreed destination.

Major engine, transmission, steering or suspension faults can make continued driving unsuitable. Recovering the vehicle instead can help you avoid attempting to drive a vehicle that may not be safe to operate.
Severely damaged wheels or tyres can prevent normal driving. Depending on the vehicle and location, flatbed transportation may be an appropriate recovery option.

settings.title: Flatbed Recovery for Damaged and Non-Running Vehicles

settings.editor:
A damaged or non-running vehicle may require different recovery arrangements from a vehicle that can still drive normally.

Before arranging recovery, tell us if:

  • The vehicle starts
  • The wheels can move
  • The steering works normally
  • Any wheels or tyres are damaged
  • There is visible accident damage
  • The vehicle is blocking access
  • The vehicle is in a restricted location

This information helps us understand the situation and discuss the appropriate recovery requirements.

Flatbed recovery can be useful for vehicles affected by engine failure, electrical faults, serious mechanical problems, accident damage, damaged wheels and other faults that prevent safe driving.
GOOD TO KNOW

Vehicle problems can happen at any time. Your car may stop late at night, become damaged during a journey or develop a fault at the weekend. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides recovery support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, subject to availability.
When contacting us, provide:

• Your exact location
  • Vehicle make and model
  • Registration number
  • Description of the problem
  • Vehicle condition
  • Whether it starts or moves
  • Your preferred destination

If your vehicle has stopped somewhere dangerous, prioritise your safety first. On motorways and high-speed roads, follow official road safety guidance and avoid moving into traffic unless it is safe. One of the common reasons for arranging flatbed recovery is transporting a vehicle to a garage. If your vehicle has broken down and cannot safely continue, you can provide the details of your preferred repair centre or another suitable destination.

When requesting recovery, tell us:

Following a collision, a vehicle may have damage that is not immediately obvious. Steering, suspension, wheels, bodywork or other components can be affected.

If your vehicle has been involved in an accident, do not assume it is safe to drive simply because the engine starts. If there is immediate danger, contact the emergency services and move yourself and passengers to a safe position where possible.

Once the situation is safe, A.A.D Transport & Recovery can discuss recovery and transportation to an agreed garage, repair centre, home or other destination.

settings.title: Common Reasons Drivers Call Us For Recovery

settings.editor: No two breakdowns are the same, but most fall into a handful of familiar categories. Here are the situations we help with most often across Birmingham:
If you're not sure exactly what's wrong, that's fine — call us, describe what's happening, and we'll talk you through whether it's safe to continue or whether recovery is the better option.

• Car won't start at home, at work, in a car park or at the roadside
  • Flat battery, failed jump start or electrical fault
  • Flat tyre, damaged wheel or tyre blowout
  • Warning lights, limp mode or sudden loss of power
  • Overheating, coolant leaks or unusual engine noises
  • Clutch, gearbox or other mechanical faults

• Running out of fuel or misfuelling
  • Vehicle involved in a collision and needs recovering from the scene
  • Van or commercial vehicle breakdown affecting a working day
  • Non-running vehicle that needs moving to a garage
  • Vehicle stuck after a motorway or major road fault
  • Locked out of your own car
